name: Census Transform Micro-Texture Analysis
description: Applies a non-parametric local spatial transform to evaluate micro-texture consistency. AI generative models, particularly diffusion-based frameworks, often fail to synthesize authentic, high-frequency textural relationships between neighboring pixels, creating statistically abnormal local binary patterns.
algorithm: Non-parametric Local Binary Pixel Census Transform
mechanism: The algorithm maps the local spatial structure around each pixel by comparing its intensity to its immediate neighborhood, generating a bit string (Census signature) that encapsulates the local micro-texture invariant to uniform brightness shifts. In authentic images, physical constraints like material texture and organic sensor noise dictate complex, naturally dispersed Census signatures. Conversely, AI-generated images display a severely restricted or repetitive vocabulary of local binary patterns due to the generalized smoothing and decoding operations inherent in convolutional image synthesis.
parameters: Detection Window: 3x3 or 5x5 Neighborhood, Feature Extraction: Local Binary Signatures, Evaluation: Intra-region Hamming distance variance
accuracy: Moderate to High (75-85%) - Extremely effective against older GANs and highly capable of identifying diffusion model artifacts on uncompressed images.
source: Zabih & Woodfill (1994) / Fridrich & Kodovsky (2012) - Advanced Steganalysis Forensics
useCase: Detecting synthetic micro-textures, identifying AI generation purely from high-frequency pixel relationships, and evaluating surface texture authenticity.

references.title: Zabih, R. & Woodfill, J. (1994). Non-parametric Local Transforms for Computing Visual Correspondence. ECCV.
Fridrich, J. & Kodovsky, J. (2012). Rich Models for Steganalysis of Digital Images. IEEE TIFS.

strengths:
• Deeply robust against global illumination changes, brightness adjustments, and basic color grading manipulations.
• Excels at detecting and mathematically highlighting the unnatural, 'plastic' micro-textures typical of AI image generators.
• Relies on computationally straightforward boolean logic with exceptionally fast execution capability.
• Operates strictly at the local pixel level, avoiding confusion from distracting macro-semantic context.
limitations:
• Forensic spatial signal is heavily degraded or permanently destroyed by moderate lossy compression (standard social media JPEGs).
• Performs poorly as a standalone tool on completely smooth, textureless surfaces lacking a baseline micro-texture.
• Very difficult to isolate synthetic AI generation from aggressive artificial upscaling or aggressive digital sharpening algorithms.
• Can occasionally trigger false alarms on highly detailed, geometrically perfect 2D patterns (like dense grids or moiré).
